questions.stem: A client with chronic kidney disease has marked hyperphosphatemia. Which additional laboratory abnormality commonly accompanies this disturbance in advanced CKD?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Hypercalcemia, because phosphate retention in chronic kidney disease usually raises serum calcium while suppressing parathyroid hormone release.","B":"Hypocalcemia, because phosphate retention and reduced calcitriol activity in chronic kidney disease can lower calcium and disrupt mineral balance.","C":"Severe hypernatremia, because impaired phosphate excretion directly causes sodium accumulation as the characteristic paired electrolyte disturbance.","D":"Isolated hypermagnesemia, because elevated phosphate is defined by a simultaneous rise in magnesium rather than a disturbance of calcium balance."}}
questions.rationale: In CKD, reduced phosphate excretion can cause hyperphosphatemia, and reduced calcitriol activity plus phosphate retention can contribute to hypocalcemia and secondary hyperparathyroidism. Option B is correct. Option A states the opposite calcium relationship. Options C and D are not the characteristic paired disturbances described in CKD mineral-bone disease.
questions.source_detail: MSD Manual Professional, updated December 2025, identifies chronic kidney disease as a major cause of hyperphosphatemia and notes that accompanying hypocalcemia can occur.

questions.stem: A client with fever and productive cough has neutrophilia with increased immature neutrophil forms. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The differential is compatible with acute infection or inflammation; with this clinical presentation, a bacterial respiratory infection is an important concern.","B":"The differential rules out bacterial infection because increased neutrophils and immature neutrophil forms are characteristic only of uncomplicated viral illness.","C":"The differential is primarily evidence of iron-deficiency anemia because neutrophil changes are not meaningfully associated with acute infectious processes.","D":"The differential is a normal finding that does not require correlation with the client's fever, respiratory symptoms, examination findings, or other testing."}}
questions.rationale: Acute infection and inflammation can increase circulating neutrophils, including immature forms; neutrophils are particularly associated with defense against bacterial infection. Option A is correct because it appropriately correlates the laboratory pattern with the client's symptoms without treating it as diagnostic by itself. Option B reverses the association. Option C incorrectly attributes the differential to anemia. Option D ignores clinically relevant abnormalities and the need for correlation.
questions.source_name: MSD Manual Professional — Manifestations of Infection
questions.source_detail: Current MSD guidance notes that infectious disease commonly increases mature and immature circulating neutrophils; interpretation should be integrated with the clinical presentation.

questions.stem: A client has an elevated prostate-specific antigen (PSA) result and assumes this confirms prostate cancer. Which explanation is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"An elevated PSA is not diagnostic by itself; prostate cancer can raise PSA, but benign enlargement, inflammation, and other factors can also increase it.","B":"An elevated PSA confirms prostate cancer by itself because benign prostate conditions and recent prostate inflammation do not meaningfully affect the result.","C":"An elevated PSA has no established clinical relevance because prostate cells do not normally produce PSA and cancer does not alter serum concentrations.","D":"An elevated PSA is considered normal in every man over age 50 regardless of the actual value, symptoms, examination, medications, or prior results."}}
questions.rationale: PSA is produced by normal and malignant prostate cells, and elevated values can occur with prostate cancer as well as benign conditions such as BPH and prostatitis. Option A is correct because an elevated PSA requires clinical interpretation and possible further evaluation rather than serving as a stand-alone diagnosis. Option B overstates specificity. Option C is false. Option D incorrectly applies an age-based blanket rule.
questions.source_name: National Cancer Institute — Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) Test
questions.source_detail: NCI states that PSA can be elevated in prostate cancer and in benign conditions such as benign prostatic hyperplasia and prostatitis; a single elevated PSA result does not by itself diagnose cancer.

questions.stem: A client being evaluated for a pelvic mass has an elevated CA-125 level and asks whether this confirms ovarian cancer. Which response is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"CA-125 is associated with ovarian cancer, but benign conditions and other malignancies can also elevate it, so the result is not diagnostic by itself.","B":"CA-125 is specific for lung cancer, so an elevated result makes an ovarian or other gynecologic source unlikely in a client with a pelvic mass.","C":"CA-125 has no recognized association with ovarian cancer and is not used as a tumor marker in evaluating or monitoring ovarian malignancy.","D":"CA-125 is specific for prostate disease, so an elevated result should be interpreted mainly as evidence of prostate pathology rather than a pelvic mass."}}
questions.rationale: CA-125 is a tumor-associated marker commonly linked with ovarian cancer, but it lacks sufficient specificity to diagnose ovarian cancer by itself because benign conditions and other cancers can also elevate it. Option A is correct. Options B and D assign CA-125 to unrelated primary disease categories. Option C incorrectly denies its established ovarian-cancer association.
questions.source_name: National Cancer Institute — Ovarian Cancer Screening (PDQ)
questions.source_detail: NCI identifies CA-125 as a tumor-associated antigen used in ovarian-cancer contexts and notes that elevated levels are not specific because benign conditions and non-gynecologic malignancies can also increase CA-125.

questions.stem: A laboratory specifically instructs a client to fast before a lipid panel. Which teaching is appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Avoid all fluids, including plain water, for a full 24 hours before the blood draw because any liquid intake invalidates fasting lipid measurements.","B":"Follow the laboratory's fasting interval, usually about 9 to 12 hours, avoiding food and caloric drinks while plain water is generally allowed.","C":"Eat a normal meal immediately before the blood draw because fasting instructions do not apply once the test is labeled as a lipid panel.","D":"Drink sweetened beverages during the fasting period because clear liquids containing calories do not affect a fasting laboratory sample."}}
questions.rationale: When fasting is required for a lipid panel, MedlinePlus advises following the specified fasting period—commonly about 9 to 12 hours—and allowing only plain water unless instructed otherwise. Option B is correct. Option A incorrectly prohibits water and extends fasting to 24 hours. Option C ignores the explicit fasting order. Option D incorrectly permits caloric beverages.
questions.source_name: MedlinePlus — Cholesterol Levels: What You Need to Know
questions.source_detail: Current MedlinePlus guidance states that a fasting lipid panel may require 9 to 12 hours without food or caloric beverages and that plain water is allowed; patients should follow the exact instructions given.
